My Skill Stack:
Crafting Digital
Solutions

Framer

Web Design

I’m proficient with Framer, using it to design and prototype interactive web experiences with a strong focus on responsive layouts and smooth user flows. I rely on Framer’s advanced features to quickly iterate, refine, and deliver production-ready designs.

Figma

Collaborative Design

Figma is my collaborative design platform of choice. I utilize it to work seamlessly with team members and clients, facilitating real-time feedback and design iterations. Its cloud-based approach streamlines the design process.

Adobe Creative Suite

Design

I have strong proficiency across the Adobe Creative Suite, with hands-on experience in Illustrator, InDesign, Photoshop, and After Effects. I use these tools daily for everything from detailed layout and vector work to image editing and motion graphics.

Generative Models

Content Generation 

I have extensive experience with generative AI, particularly with GPT and Google Gemini. My workflow includes deep research, reasoning models, and a range of other AI tools, allowing me to efficiently gather insights and develop innovative solutions.

HTML 5

Structure and Content

HTML5 is the backbone of my web design work. I use it to structure content, making sure that every website I build is clear, accessible, and easy to navigate. It lays the groundwork for all visual elements and allows me to incorporate the latest features and practices in web development.

Topaz AI Suite

Content Enhancement

I have solid experience with the Topaz AI Suite, using its advanced tools for image upscaling, noise reduction, and sharpening to consistently deliver crisp, high-quality visuals. These AI enhancements help me elevate the look of both digital and print work, making my projects stand out.

Ableton Live Suite

Sound Design and Music

Ableton Live is my go-to platform for music production and sound design. I use it to compose, arrange, and experiment with audio, leveraging its powerful tools and intuitive workflow to craft unique sounds, remixes, and polished tracks for both personal projects and live DJ sets.

Blender

3D Motion Graphics

Blender is my preferred tool for 3D design and motion graphics, allowing me to create everything from detailed models to dynamic scenes. I use it to experiment with lighting, textures, and animation, bringing creative concepts to life for both visual projects and multimedia work.

Trendless: A Human-Centred Design Project
Overview

Trendless is a nonprofit awareness initiative and browser plugin designed to interrupt the cycle of social media micro-trends and hyper-consumerism. Built over seven weeks as part of a UI / UX design course at Algonquin College. 

The Problem

Social media has evolved into a mass-scale engine for algorithmic spread, where aesthetics and products can explode in popularity almost overnight. The problem is systemic - accessible, low-cost items get pushed to enormous audiences, triggering participation not out of genuine desire but out of FOMO and the pursuit of belonging. Trends burn bright for weeks or months, then collapse, leaving consumers with products they no longer want and a compulsion to chase whatever comes next. The cycle produces real consequences: financial strain from continuous low-stakes purchases that accumulate, significant environmental waste from the rapid disposal of short-lifespan goods, and a gradual loss of personal identity as style and self-expression conform to whatever the algorithm is currently rewarding.

Research & Discovery

We defined two primary personas. Athena, a 19-year-old navigating early adulthood and a recent BPD diagnosis, who relies on trend participation for a sense of community and belonging. And Zara, a full-time Vancouver content creator financially trapped in a cycle of buying and discarding products to maintain sponsor-worthy engagement numbers. Both users represent opposite ends of the same system, one consuming, one supplying, and both losing something in the process.

To pressure test our direction, we ran a focus group with five participants. The findings validated our core assumptions: most people struggle to identify undisclosed ads, nearly everyone expressed interest in a plugin that could flag sponsored content, and the consensus on checkout friction was positive, provided it came with customization options to avoid feeling punitive.

Design Principles

Three principles anchored every decision we made:

Raise awareness on the personal impact of micro-trends

Design friction to disrupt the "buy now" dopamine loop

Decouple social relevance from material consumption

The Solution

Trendless operates as a three part system. A social media campaign uses the visual language of trending content to catch the target demographic mid-scroll; meeting them in the space where the problem lives. The campaign drives traffic to a website that serves as the initiative's hub: transparent about its mission, educational in its content, and trustworthy enough to convert visitors into plugin users.

The plugin itself is the core intervention. While a user scrolls, it actively surfaces undisclosed ads and sponsored content with a non-intrusive notification; making influence visible rather than invisible. At checkout, it introduces a brief, customizable micro-delay with a single prompt: Does this fit your life, or just your cart? The delay is short enough not to obstruct genuine purchases, but long enough to break the automated reflex of impulse buying. Both the pop-up format and the checkout timer are fully user-adjustable, a direct response to focus group concern about friction becoming annoyance.

The bold visual identity deliberately borrows from the aesthetic register of the platforms it's critiquing.

Chasing Greatness - ECommerce Website

New Website

My Approach

I set out to make the website simple, inviting, and visually strong without making things complicated. The focus was on good navigation and clear product pages, letting the photography and stories do most of the work. Every choice was about getting people from the home page to checkout as smoothly as possible, while giving them a sense of why these books matter.

Vision and Innovation

This redesign was about moving Novak Books from a basic online shop to something that feels more like a modern tennis brand. I used Shopify’s tools to keep things fast and reliable, brought in bold fonts and crisp images, and added subtle animations for a polished feel. The Chasing Greatness series isn’t just a product—it’s part of a bigger story, and the site now reflects that.

Identifying Unique Challenges

Going from one-player focus to a series about tennis history meant we had to rethink the navigation and how products are shown. The challenge was to open up the brand to new stories without losing loyal customers. My solution was to build flexible sections that highlight Novak, introduce new players, and make sure returning visitors still feel at home.

Resolving Complex Problems

Customizing Shopify let us manage lots of different product versions, handle pre-orders, and set up collections for the new releases. I made sure the checkout was as simple as possible, set up features like inventory tracking and abandoned cart recovery, and organized everything so it’s easy for the team to update as new books come out.

User-Centric Design

Everything here is designed for real tennis fans—people who care about the game, the stories, and the details. I kept layouts simple, used lots of high-quality photos, and made sure the site works just as well on your phone as on a computer. There are product recommendations, clear CTAs, and space for excerpts so visitors get a real taste of each edition.

Novak Tennis Book Series: Serbian Edition Typesetting




Novak Bookstore

Overview

For the original Novak Djokovic tennis book series, my main responsibility was typesetting all seven volumes of the Serbian edition. The project called for a focus on clarity, consistency, and visual appeal across a substantial body of work, ensuring each book was easy to read and true to the brand’s spirit.

My Approach

I managed the entire typesetting process, carefully organizing chapter structures, headings, and text flows to maintain a cohesive look from start to finish. Special attention was paid to typography, spacing, and layout, balancing readability with a sense of elegance that matched the significance of Novak’s story.

Vision and Execution

The goal was to create an inviting reading experience for Serbian tennis fans and collectors, respecting both the content’s cultural importance and the expectations of a high-quality sports publication. My work ensured that every page felt accessible and visually balanced, from the opening dedication to the closing statistics.

Challenges and Solutions

With seven books to handle, maintaining consistency was a key challenge. I developed and applied a unified typesetting style guide, streamlining the process while making it easy to adapt layouts for each unique volume.






The final Serbian series delivers a polished, professional collection that captures Novak’s legacy, making these books a valued addition to any tennis fan’s library.

Sol de Fuego Cocina: Menu Design




Overview

For Sol de Fuego Cocina, a vibrant Latin-inspired restaurant, I created a comprehensive and visually engaging menu designed to enhance the dining experience while reflecting the establishment’s sultry, stylish character. The menu was crafted to be welcoming, easy to navigate, and aligned closely with the restaurant’s lively atmosphere and authentic Latin culinary offerings.

My Approach

I started by researching the restaurant’s style and identity, identifying themes that resonate with its Latin roots and modern approach. Leveraging Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop, I carefully selected harmonious typefaces and developed a clear type hierarchy to ensure readability and ease of use. I strategically paired decorative elements and subtle graphics, such as a sombrero illustration and sunburst motifs, with warm and inviting colors to enhance visual appeal without overwhelming diners.

Vision and Execution

My goal was to create more than just a functional menu; it was about designing an immersive, sensory experience reflective of the restaurant’s vibrant culture. By integrating thematic graphics, a restrained yet bold colour scheme, and meticulously crafted type pairings, the menu clearly communicates the restaurant’s unique offerings, enticing diners to explore and enjoy the full breadth of the cuisine.

Challenges and Solutions

One key challenge was balancing creativity with functionality to ensure diners could effortlessly navigate the extensive menu offerings. To solve this, I structured the content using intuitive layouts, clear category delineations, and careful typographic treatments, highlighting specials and key dishes prominently to enhance sales potential and diner satisfaction.

User-Centric Design

The menu design prioritized the diner’s experience by utilizing strategic white space, thoughtfully placed visuals, and accessible typography. This allowed diners to quickly find information, enhancing their comfort and enjoyment while dining.

Meeting Project Requirements

My design fulfilled all project requirements, including the integration of restaurant-specific content, menu item modifiers, and carefully chosen typography from Adobe Fonts. Additionally, I adhered strictly to technical guidelines—ensuring print readiness, file organization, and compliance with CMYK standards for professional-quality production.

Final Result

The finished Sol de Fuego Cocina menu is visually compelling, clear, and fully functional—perfectly aligned with the restaurant’s vibrant Latin theme. It serves both practical and aesthetic purposes, contributing positively to diners’ experiences and the restaurant’s overall branding efforts.

Beatport Redesign

A comprehensive UI/UX and brand refresh for Beatport, the world’s leading music platform for DJs and producers. This project was completed as a capstone for Web Design 3, with a focus on creating a seamless, visually compelling, and intuitive digital experience that better serves Beatport’s global community.

My Approach

My redesign of Beatport was rooted in a detailed discovery phase, including a thorough audit of the current site, analysis of user needs, and competitive benchmarking within the digital music landscape. I identified key pain points: outdated visual identity, cluttered navigation, poor responsiveness, and a lack of cohesive UI scaling across devices. Leveraging this research, I established a bold new direction anchored in a dark, high-contrast palette and a vibrant neon accent (01FF95) to evoke the energy of club culture.

Key steps included:

Content Audit & Structure: Streamlined the navigation and site architecture for easier access to featured tracks, trending artists, and playlists.

Visual Language: Developed a unified style guide featuring Gravita GEO as the primary typeface, custom icons, and a modern button system.

Moodboard Development: Gathered visual inspiration from music tech, nightlife, and retro-futurism, setting the tone for immersive discovery.

Vision and Innovation

Beatport’s community is passionate, global, and highly engaged. My vision was to transform the platform into a more intuitive, visually dynamic, and responsive experience that bridges the gap between digital browsing and the excitement of crate-digging in a record shop. I placed strong emphasis on:

Immersive Discovery: High-visibility “Album of the Week,” bold cover art, and integrated streaming/buy options surface new releases while keeping users in flow.

Accessibility & Performance: Improved hierarchy, larger touch targets, and simplified navigation ensure seamless usability across all devices.

Brand Cohesion: Neon green highlights and a consistent icon system reinforce Beatport’s identity while updating its look for a new generation.

Identifying Unique Challenges

The biggest challenge was balancing Beatport’s extensive catalog and feature set with the need for clarity and speed. The legacy UI was dense and overwhelming, so I prioritized a content structure that delivers core features—music discovery, streaming, downloads—in just a few clicks. The redesign involved stripping away distractions, focusing on user journeys, and future-proofing the design for mobile and desktop use. Achieving a balance between bold, energetic visuals and functional minimalism was central to this process.

This project showcases my end-to-end UX process: from research, strategy, and moodboarding to UI system development and high-fidelity prototyping. The result is a Beatport experience that feels both fresh and familiar—energizing for DJs, accessible to newcomers, and built to scale for the future of digital music.

ToldYa - Tennis Application

ToldYa brings the thrill of tennis predictions to life, offering fans a fresh, interactive way to engage with matches and friends. Designed for tennis enthusiasts who crave both competition and community, ToldYa transforms the spectator experience into a dynamic, social game.

ToldYa is available on the App Store and Google Play, with features best enjoyed by users who create an account and join in weekly predictions and challenges.

My Approach

As part of the ToldYa team, my role focused on enhancing the app’s user experience and supporting technical operations. I contributed to the design of intuitive wireframes and interactive prototypes using Figma, helping to create an interface that makes complex match data easy and fun to explore. On the technical side, I assisted in asset management and supported backend operations, including Amazon AWS server management, to ensure reliability during peak usage.

Vision and Innovation

ToldYa’s vision is to transform how fans interact with tennis—making match predictions a shared, social experience. By integrating competitive gameplay, leaderboards, and community features, the app brings a sense of excitement and camaraderie to every match.

Identifying Unique Challenges

Balancing real-time sports data with an approachable user interface was a major challenge. My contributions included helping organize and present live match schedules, prediction features, and results in a way that remained clear and engaging for users.

Resolving Complex Problems

I supported backend operations to ensure the app could scale efficiently and maintain fast performance during high-traffic events. By assisting with asset management and server maintenance on AWS, I contributed to the stability and smooth operation of the app’s core features.

User-Centric Design

Every design and development decision aimed to put users first—making navigation simple, feedback instant, and interactions enjoyable. I worked to ensure that ToldYa remained accessible, responsive, and engaging for all users.

Meeting User Needs

ToldYa stands out by offering more than scores and schedules: it invites users to predict, compete, and share in the thrill of the game. My work helped shape an experience where users feel included and excited to participate, whether they’re seasoned tennis fans or casual spectators.

Home: Highlights key matches and user activity.

Predict: Streamlined prediction flow for upcoming matches.

Challenges: Tools to invite friends and compete head-to-head.

Leaderboard: Showcases community standings and achievements.

Profile: Personal stats, progress, and settings.

Accessibility and Optimization

With accessibility in mind, ToldYa features high-contrast visuals, intuitive navigation, and performance enhancements for smooth operation across devices and conditions.

Conclusion

My experience with ToldYa gave me the opportunity to blend UX design and backend operations in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. By focusing on usability, reliability, and community, I helped deliver an app that redefines how tennis fans engage with their sport—turning every match into a shared, interactive event.

ToldYa - Tennis Application

Client

HintonX

Duration

6 Months

Category

UX

ToldYa brings the thrill of tennis predictions to life, offering fans a fresh, interactive way to engage with matches and friends. Designed for tennis enthusiasts who crave both competition and community, ToldYa transforms the spectator experience into a dynamic, social game.

ToldYa is available on the App Store and Google Play, with features best enjoyed by users who create an account and join in weekly predictions and challenges.

My Approach

As part of the ToldYa team, my role focused on enhancing the app’s user experience and supporting technical operations. I contributed to the design of intuitive wireframes and interactive prototypes using Figma, helping to create an interface that makes complex match data easy and fun to explore. On the technical side, I assisted in asset management and supported backend operations, including Amazon AWS server management, to ensure reliability during peak usage.

Vision and Innovation

ToldYa’s vision is to transform how fans interact with tennis—making match predictions a shared, social experience. By integrating competitive gameplay, leaderboards, and community features, the app brings a sense of excitement and camaraderie to every match.

Identifying Unique Challenges

Balancing real-time sports data with an approachable user interface was a major challenge. My contributions included helping organize and present live match schedules, prediction features, and results in a way that remained clear and engaging for users.

Resolving Complex Problems

I supported backend operations to ensure the app could scale efficiently and maintain fast performance during high-traffic events. By assisting with asset management and server maintenance on AWS, I contributed to the stability and smooth operation of the app’s core features.

User-Centric Design

Every design and development decision aimed to put users first—making navigation simple, feedback instant, and interactions enjoyable. I worked to ensure that ToldYa remained accessible, responsive, and engaging for all users.

Meeting User Needs

ToldYa stands out by offering more than scores and schedules: it invites users to predict, compete, and share in the thrill of the game. My work helped shape an experience where users feel included and excited to participate, whether they’re seasoned tennis fans or casual spectators.

Home: Highlights key matches and user activity.

Predict: Streamlined prediction flow for upcoming matches.

Challenges: Tools to invite friends and compete head-to-head.

Leaderboard: Showcases community standings and achievements.

Profile: Personal stats, progress, and settings.

Accessibility and Optimization

With accessibility in mind, ToldYa features high-contrast visuals, intuitive navigation, and performance enhancements for smooth operation across devices and conditions.

Conclusion

My experience with ToldYa gave me the opportunity to blend UX design and backend operations in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. By focusing on usability, reliability, and community, I helped deliver an app that redefines how tennis fans engage with their sport—turning every match into a shared, interactive event.
